Public land swap deals in which the government takes property from one private owner to trade land with a different private owner violates property ownership rights, the New Jersey Supreme Court ruled Monday. Even though New Jersey aligns with a broad federal understanding of eminent domain powers, the condemnation of land without applying that specific land for a public use violates the federal and state constitutions, Chief Justice Stuart Rabner wrote for the unanimous court. “Why didn’t the town condemn the developer’s land outright or exchange land the town already owned?” Rabner wrote. fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # SK Hynix Billionaire Ordered To Pay $645 Million Divorce Settlement—Korea’s Largest Ever. South Korean billionaire and SK Group chair Chey Tae-won was ordered to pay his ex-wife around $645 million, in the country’s largest-ever divorce settlement, putting a significant dent in the billionaire’s personal fortune, which has soared this year amid an AI-driven boom in the prices of advanced memory chips sold by his company SK Hynix. According to South Korea’s Yonhap News Agency, a Seoul appeals court ruled that Chey must pay his former wife, Roh Soh-yeong, a property division settlement of KRW 944 billion ($645.7 million). The payout is Korea’s largest-ever divorce settlement but is lower than the KRW 1.38 trillion (around $945 million) that a court had initially granted to Roh in 2024—but later overturned by the country’s Supreme Court. The court dismissed Chey’s argument that his holdings of SK Inc.’s shares should not be part of the settlement, as he had inherited them, and ruled that Roh was entitled to one-third of the couple’s joint property.

(WO) — **Vitol** has agreed to sell its U.S. upstream company, **VTX Energy Partners**, to Houston-based **Verde Operating Company** for an undisclosed amount, the companies announced. Formed in 2022 by Vitol and the former ATX Energy management team led by Gene Shepherd and Erik Hoover, VTX has grown into a significant producer in the southern Delaware basin. Shepherd said the transaction marks the next stage of the company's growth. "I would like to thank Vitol for the opportunity of building VTX into the successful business it is today," Shepherd said. "It is a great time for U.S. energy, and I am really excited by the next chapter for VTX with Verde.".

Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has signed a pact with venture capital firms Thinkuvate and ValleyNXT to invest up to ₹10 crore in student-led startups. This initiative aims to support early-stage ventures in sectors like deep tech, fintech, and healthcare. Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT) has officially partnered with venture capital firms Thinkuvate and ValleyNXT to launch a new funding initiative for student-led startups. Under this agreement, a total of ₹10 crore has been earmarked to support early-stage companies founded by students on campus. While this initiative provides a platform for student-led companies, the actual financial impact on the broader startup ecosystem will depend on the successful commercialization of these ventures. The key monitorable will be the success rate of the ventures funded under this specific ₹10 crore pool and how it influences the future pipeline of technology-driven businesses coming out of the VIT campus.
